summary: ADR-004 declares a cache-first read path with no cache above the storefront — amend the ADR to what exists
description:
### Finding (architecture review R4, 2026-07-25)

ADR-004 declares volatility-tiered TTLs with one cache owner per tier. Verified against the code:

- **The only cache that exists** is `web/storefront/src/lib/cache.ts` — an in-process Astro SSR page-data map with single-flight coalescing. It is correct, and it does honor the tier (the middleware derives the outgoing `Cache-Control` from *remaining* freshness, so staleness does not stack).
- **The gateway does not cache.** `gateway/cmd/gateway/main.go` builds a bare `httputil.ReverseProxy` per route. Nothing between it and the services caches anything.
- **Back-office, scanner and service-to-service reads honor no cache at all.** They receive `Cache-Control: public, max-age=300` and discard it.

So `Cache-Control` on the service side is presently a declaration with no consumer outside SSR. That is a defensible position — the headers are exactly the contract a future tier needs — but the ADR does not say so, and a reader reasonably concludes a cache tier is deployed.

### Scope discipline

**Docs only.** Building the tier is TKT-31's epic (Read-path caching & hot-event serving). This ticket must not grow a code diff — a source change in the PR is a scope failure, not a bonus.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] ADR-004 states which readers honor the volatility tiers today (SSR page-data cache, with single-flight) and which honor nothing (gateway, service-to-service, back-office, scanner).
- [ ] It states that the TTL declarations are a contract for future caches, so the next reader does not mistake them for a deployed tier.
- [ ] The gap is linked to TKT-31, not left implicit.
- [ ] `docs/architecture.md`'s caching line matches.
- [ ] The diff contains **no source changes**.

objective.note: ADR-004 reads as if a cache tier exists. It does not: the only cache honoring the TTL declarations is the Astro SSR page-data cache in one process. Make the ADR describe what is true, and route the actual gap to the epic that owns it.

scope.note: IN: amending ADR-004 to state exactly which readers honor the volatility tiers today and which do not; correcting the caching line in docs/architecture.md; linking the gap to TKT-31. OUT: building any cache (that is TKT-31); changing any Cache-Control header or TTL value; any code change at all.

uncertainties.note: None. This is a documentation correction against read code; the facts were verified in this review (gateway/cmd/gateway/main.go has no cache; web/storefront/src/lib/cache.ts is the only implementation).

dependencies.note: None. Relates to TKT-31 (Epic: Read-path caching & hot-event serving), which owns the actual tier — linked, not blocking.

approach.note: Amend, do not rewrite: the TTL tiers and the single-cache-owner rule are still the right decisions and stay. What changes is the ADR saying plainly that the tiers are today a contract for future caches and bind only the SSR tier. Docs and ADR only — no source changes (this ticket must not grow a code diff).

first_slice.note: The whole ticket is one slice: the ADR-004 amendment plus the architecture.md line. Small enough for risk:low.

success.note: COS: (1) ADR-004 states which readers honor the volatility tiers today — the Astro SSR page-data cache, with single-flight — and that gateway, service-to-service, back-office and scanner reads honor nothing; (2) it says the TTL declarations are a contract for future caches, so no future reader mistakes them for an existing tier; (3) the gap is linked to TKT-31 rather than left implicit; (4) docs/architecture.md's caching line matches; (5) zero source changes in the diff.

context_memo.note: Baked: ADR-004 (the decision being amended — the tiers and the single-owner rule survive, only the claim about coverage changes), ADR-006 (the storefront shell owns the minutes tier — the one place the rule IS implemented, and the model for how the ADR should read). Related epic: TKT-31 read-path caching & hot-event serving.

binding.rule: Public reads declare volatility-tiered TTLs; the read path is cache-first, and each tier has exactly one cache owner so staleness never stacks.

We build five Go services (catalog, inventory, commerce, payments, access) behind an API gateway, with an event bus for the domain event stream; every entity carries a tenant/organizer id from day one. Docker Compose only. The gateway is the only public surface, with explicit route registration.

---

### One correction to the ticket's own references, found at claim time

The ticket's `context.reference` and its description both link
`docs/reviews/2026-07-25-architecture.md`. **That file does not exist** — not on `main`, not on the
`arch-review-in-place` branch, not anywhere in history (`git log --all --diff-filter=A -- 'docs/reviews/*'`
returns nothing; `docs/reviews/` is not a directory in this repo). The R4 architecture review was
conducted in-session and its findings were written straight into tickets, never into a review file.

Consequence for the work: the amended ADR-004 **must not cite that path** — a dead link in a decision
record is worse than no link. The provenance will be cited as TKT-128 (and TKT-31 for the gap),
which are real and resolvable. Carried into the plan brief as a constraint.

<!-- sdlc:stage=planning kind=plan -->
### Plan draft — TKT-128

**Drafted by `gpt-5.6-sol`** (codex companion, `task --effort high`, read-only — no `--write`), per
`config.models.plan`. Session `019fa951-cbe3-7bf0-9def-2e8d796d765c`, 210s. Verbatim below; the
critique (`config.models.planReview` = `main-agent`) follows as `kind=plan-final`.

Brief given to the drafter included the re-resolved governing-ADR section (ADR-004 subject, ADR-019
form constraint, ADR-006 the one implementation, ADR-009 the contract framing) and the claim-time
finding that `docs/reviews/2026-07-25-architecture.md` does not exist.

---

## 1. Definition of Done

- [COS 1] ADR-004 contains a dated amendment that distinguishes the accepted design from current implementation coverage:
  - The only application cache is the storefront’s process-local Astro SSR page-data cache.
  - It caches only the minutes-tier event-list, event-detail, and festival-detail reads currently routed through `pageRead`.
  - It uses upstream `max-age`, coalesces concurrent misses with single-flight, and exposes remaining freshness to middleware so page-response staleness does not stack.
  - The gateway, service-to-service clients, back office, and scanner have no cache layer that consumes positive TTL declarations.
  - Scanner scan/reconcile operations are in the never-cached tier, so their lack of caching is correct, not an implementation gap.
  - ADR-004 rule 2—service-side in-memory hot-event structures—is explicitly recorded as unimplemented.
- [COS 2] The amendment states that TTL declarations remain an active API-design contract for future caches; they must not be interpreted as evidence that a gateway, CDN, reverse-proxy, or service cache is deployed.
- [COS 3] All undeployed cache tiers and service-side hot-event serving are explicitly assigned to **TKT-31 — Read-path caching & hot-event serving**.
- [COS 4] The caching invariant at [docs/architecture.md:88](/Users/matdupui/Sources/Mathieu/ticketing_system.arch-review-in-place/docs/architecture.md:88) summarizes the same current coverage, prospective contract, and TKT-31 ownership.
- [COS 5] The final branch diff against `origin/main` contains exactly the two documentation files below and no source, generated, configuration, test, or tooling changes.
- ADR-004’s original three rules at [ADR-004:32](/Users/matdupui/Sources/Mathieu/ticketing_system.arch-review-in-place/docs/adr/ADR-004-cache-first-read-path.md:32) remain normative. The amendment clarifies implementation status; it does not weaken, replace, or rewrite the 2026-07-12 decision.
- The existing ADR-019 Status pointer at [ADR-004:9](/Users/matdupui/Sources/Mathieu/ticketing_system.arch-review-in-place/docs/adr/ADR-004-cache-first-read-path.md:9) and ADR-019’s reciprocal reference at [ADR-019:205](/Users/matdupui/Sources/Mathieu/ticketing_system.arch-review-in-place/docs/adr/ADR-019-catalog-read-path-scoping.md:205) remain intact.

## 2. Files touched

- `docs/adr/ADR-004-cache-first-read-path.md`
  - Add a short Status pointer and a substantive dated amendment.
  - Update References with TKT-128 provenance, explicit TKT-31 ownership, ADR-006, ADR-009, and the relevant implementation seams.
  - Estimated change: approximately 25–32 added lines; no rewriting of the original Context, Decision, or Consequences.
- `docs/architecture.md`
  - Replace the current two-line caching invariant at lines 88–89 with approximately three or four lines that summarize declared TTLs, current SSR-only consumption, absent tiers, and TKT-31 ownership.
  - Estimated change: replace 2 lines with 3–4 lines, net approximately +1–2.

No listed path is uncertain. No other file should be touched.

The following are evidence only and must remain unchanged:

- [web/storefront/src/lib/cache.ts:39](/Users/matdupui/Sources/Mathieu/ticketing_system.arch-review-in-place/web/storefront/src/lib/cache.ts:39)
- [web/storefront/src/lib/api.ts:17](/Users/matdupui/Sources/Mathieu/ticketing_system.arch-review-in-place/web/storefront/src/lib/api.ts:17)
- [web/storefront/src/middleware.ts:15](/Users/matdupui/Sources/Mathieu/ticketing_system.arch-review-in-place/web/storefront/src/middleware.ts:15)
- [gateway/cmd/gateway/main.go:176](/Users/matdupui/Sources/Mathieu/ticketing_system.arch-review-in-place/gateway/cmd/gateway/main.go:176)
- [services/catalog/api/openapi.yaml:678](/Users/matdupui/Sources/Mathieu/ticketing_system.arch-review-in-place/services/catalog/api/openapi.yaml:678)
- [web/backoffice/src/lib/api.ts:37](/Users/matdupui/Sources/Mathieu/ticketing_system.arch-review-in-place/web/backoffice/src/lib/api.ts:37)
- [web/scanner/src/App.tsx:80](/Users/matdupui/Sources/Mathieu/ticketing_system.arch-review-in-place/web/scanner/src/App.tsx:80)

## 3. The amendment's shape

Preserve the existing `## Status` content, especially the complete “Extended by ADR-019” paragraph at lines 9–12. Immediately after it, add a short pointer following ADR-028’s pattern at [ADR-028:9](/Users/matdupui/Sources/Mathieu/ticketing_system.arch-review-in-place/docs/adr/ADR-028-response-drift-fail-closed.md:9):

> *Amended by TKT-128 (2026-07-28): the decision remains the target architecture; the amendment records which cache tiers are actually implemented today. See § Amendment (TKT-128).*

Then add the substantive section after `## Consequences` and before `## References`, matching the placement used by [ADR-005:38](/Users/matdupui/Sources/Mathieu/ticketing_system.arch-review-in-place/docs/adr/ADR-005-unified-dated-slot-admission.md:38) and [ADR-028:82](/Users/matdupui/Sources/Mathieu/ticketing_system.arch-review-in-place/docs/adr/ADR-028-response-drift-fail-closed.md:82):

`## Amendment (TKT-128, 2026-07-28) — actual cache coverage`

The section should make these claims:

1. **Decision versus deployment.** The three original rules remain accepted design constraints. As of the amendment date, they are not a description of a fully deployed cache-first topology.

2. **The declarations remain real contracts.** Public read TTLs are committed in the contract-first OpenAPI source, not merely incidental runtime headers. ADR-009 makes the OpenAPI document authoritative and gate-diffed at [ADR-009:34](/Users/matdupui/Sources/Mathieu/ticketing_system.arch-review-in-place/docs/adr/ADR-009-contract-first-apis.md:34); catalog operations declare the minutes and hours tiers at [openapi.yaml:678](/Users/matdupui/Sources/Mathieu/ticketing_system.arch-review-in-place/services/catalog/api/openapi.yaml:678) onward. Therefore:
   - The TTLs are an active contract that future cache owners must honor.
   - Header emission does not prove that such an owner is currently deployed.
   - Do not call the headers “dead”; they preserve the API shape required by TKT-31.

3. **Exact current cache coverage.**
   - `web/storefront/src/lib/api.ts` owns one module-level `PageDataCache` and sends only event-list, event-detail, and festival-detail reads through it at [api.ts:17](/Users/matdupui/Sources/Mathieu/ticketing_system.arch-review-in-place/web/storefront/src/lib/api.ts:17) and [api.ts:29](/Users/matdupui/Sources/Mathieu/ticketing_system.arch-review-in-place/web/storefront/src/lib/api.ts:29).
   - The cache is process-local, URL-keyed, fetch-through, governed by upstream `max-age`, and coalesces concurrent same-key misses at [cache.ts:39](/Users/matdupui/Sources/Mathieu/ticketing_system.arch-review-in-place/web/storefront/src/lib/cache.ts:39).
   - Middleware derives outgoing `Cache-Control` from remaining freshness at [middleware.ts:15](/Users/matdupui/Sources/Mathieu/ticketing_system.arch-review-in-place/web/storefront/src/middleware.ts:15), preventing the SSR data age and a later page cache age from exceeding the tier in aggregate.
   - Cross-reference ADR-006’s caching-ownership rule at [ADR-006:48](/Users/matdupui/Sources/Mathieu/ticketing_system.arch-review-in-place/docs/adr/ADR-006-astro-storefront-shell.md:48).

4. **Explicit non-coverage.**
   - The gateway is a bare `httputil.ReverseProxy` at [main.go:179](/Users/matdupui/Sources/Mathieu/ticketing_system.arch-review-in-place/gateway/cmd/gateway/main.go:179); it forwards responses but owns no cache.
   - Back-office reads use bare `fetch`, including the positive hours-tier venue and seat-map reads at [api.ts:37](/Users/matdupui/Sources/Mathieu/ticketing_system.arch-review-in-place/web/backoffice/src/lib/api.ts:37) and [api.ts:134](/Users/matdupui/Sources/Mathieu/ticketing_system.arch-review-in-place/web/backoffice/src/lib/api.ts:134).
   - Service-to-service HTTP clients do not cache or consume TTLs; for example, Inventory performs direct catalog requests at [catalog.go:65](/Users/matdupui/Sources/Mathieu/ticketing_system.arch-review-in-place/services/inventory/internal/consumer/catalog.go:65).
   - Scanner has no cache layer, but its current scan and reconcile operations are POSTs at [App.tsx:80](/Users/matdupui/Sources/Mathieu/ticketing_system.arch-review-in-place/web/scanner/src/App.tsx:80), within ADR-004’s never-cached transactional tier. Do not present this as missing positive-TTL coverage.
   - No shared page cache, gateway cache, CDN, or reverse-proxy cache is deployed.

5. **Rule 2 is also unimplemented.** This belongs in the same amendment because it is another mismatch between ADR-004’s accepted target and current implementation. Catalog public reads still call the database-backed store directly before emitting `Cache-Control`, as illustrated at [server.go:910](/Users/matdupui/Sources/Mathieu/ticketing_system.arch-review-in-place/services/catalog/internal/api/server.go:910); Inventory availability likewise calls its PostgreSQL store directly at [server.go:237](/Users/matdupui/Sources/Mathieu/ticketing_system.arch-review-in-place/services/inventory/internal/api/server.go:237). Record that no service currently maintains the rule-2 hot-event snapshots or availability counters in memory.

6. **Ownership of the gap.** End by assigning the gateway/shared tiers, faster-than-page API tier, service in-memory structures, invalidation, kill-switch, staleness tests, and on-sale read-load evidence to **TKT-31**. The existing PRD description at [prd-v1.md:56](/Users/matdupui/Sources/Mathieu/ticketing_system.arch-review-in-place/docs/product/prd-v1.md:56) already defines that scope.

A suitable central sentence is:

> The volatility tiers remain the contract every future cache owner must implement; they are not evidence that such a tier is deployed. Today, only the storefront’s process-local SSR page-data cache consumes a positive tier, and only for its minutes-tier event and festival page reads.

This preserves the decision while making deployment status unambiguous.

## 4. Test plan / verification seam

There is no meaningful executable test for the prose’s architectural accuracy. The verification seam is a focused documentation review against the named implementation evidence.

- Confirm the amendment names only the three reads actually routed through `pageRead`; do not generalize it to every storefront route, all catalog reads, the hours tier, availability, or HTML storage.
- Confirm it separately states that rule 2 is unimplemented and TKT-31-owned.
- Confirm the architecture summary and ADR amendment make the same claims.
- Resolve every new Markdown link and verify ADR-004’s existing ADR-019 link remains unchanged.
- Confirm the nonexistent `docs/reviews/2026-07-25-architecture.md` path appears nowhere in the diff.
- Run the normal repository gate:

```sh
make check
```

This only establishes that the documentation change did not disturb the repository gate; it does not validate the prose.

Mechanically verify COS 5 after committing:

```sh
git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD
git diff --exit-code origin/main...HEAD -- . ':(exclude)docs/**'
git status --short
```

The first command must print exactly:

```text
docs/adr/ADR-004-cache-first-read-path.md
docs/architecture.md
```

The second must exit successfully with no output, and `git status --short` must be empty. Before committing, use `git diff --name-only origin/main --` plus `git status --short` to inspect staged, unstaged, and untracked paths.

Do not add an automated cache-coverage or documentation test. Such a test would be speculative tooling, would itself violate this ticket’s docs-only scope, and would still need implementation-specific heuristics to prove a prose claim.

## 5. Risks and traps

- **Scope creep into implementation:** adding a gateway cache, changing fetch behavior, changing headers, altering TTL values, adding tests, or adding lint/tooling is a COS 5 failure. TKT-31 owns the implementation.
- **Retroactively rewriting ADR-004:** do not edit the original Decision into past-tense implementation commentary. ADR-019 explicitly rejected folding later evidence into ADR-004 at [ADR-019:47](/Users/matdupui/Sources/Mathieu/ticketing_system.arch-review-in-place/docs/adr/ADR-019-catalog-read-path-scoping.md:47). A dated amendment records the new factual understanding without pretending it was part of the 2026-07-12 gate.
- **Damaging the ADR-019 relationship:** preserve the Status pointer at ADR-004 lines 9–12 and ADR-019’s miss-path distinction. Cache-hit intent and indexed miss-path cost remain separate decisions.
- **Over-claiming SSR coverage:** the current cache stores upstream JSON page data, not all SSR output. It covers event list, event detail, and festival detail only. There is no current storefront season page, hours-tier seat-map cache, or seconds-tier availability cache.
- **Repeating spike topology as deployed topology:** ADR-006’s spike demonstrated nginx HTML reuse at [ADR-006:48](/Users/matdupui/Sources/Mathieu/ticketing_system.arch-review-in-place/docs/adr/ADR-006-astro-storefront-shell.md:48). That evidence proves the shell design, not that nginx or a shared HTML cache exists in the current Compose topology.
- **Conflating header declaration with cache consumption:** services emitting `Cache-Control` and generated TypeScript carrying the description prove a contract, not a deployed cache.
- **Misclassifying scanner behavior:** scanner honors no cache, but its current scan/reconcile requests are transactional POSTs that should remain uncached. Do not list scanner as missing an hours/minutes-tier cache.
- **Weakening rule 2:** say “accepted but not implemented; TKT-31 owns it,” not “obsolete,” “optional,” or “replaced by SSR.”
- **Claiming global absence too broadly:** phrase absence as “no application/deployed cache tier in this repository” rather than making claims about browser defaults or infrastructure outside the documented topology.
- **Dead provenance link:** `docs/reviews/2026-07-25-architecture.md` and `docs/reviews/` do not exist. Do not cite or plan to create them. Cite TKT-128 for provenance and TKT-31 for remediation ownership.
- **Incorrect ADR-006 wording:** use ADR-006 for the page/API ownership and single-source discipline, but describe current code more narrowly than the spike’s intended full tier ownership.
- **Noise in References:** retain the existing brief, PRD, and ADR-002 references. Add only references needed to establish current coverage and contract provenance.

## 6. Open decisions

- None. The repository evidence resolves amendment form, placement, current cache coverage, rule-2 status, and ownership of the remaining work. The recommended implementation is the additive Status pointer plus dated post-Consequences amendment described above.
